title: Blueberry Pancakes
changes_from_base: Milk soured with lemon juice stands in for buttermilk and soured cream, and blueberries are scattered over each pancake in the pan.
summary: Light, tender pancakes with bright bursts of tart blueberries throughout, lifted by a whisper of lemon.
equipment: nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
blueberries, fresh or frozen (ideally wild), rinsed and dried

steps.title: Sour milk
steps.text: Whisk 1 tbsp lemon juice into 480 ml milk and set aside to thicken.

steps.title: Mix dry
steps.text: Whisk 283 g plain flour, 2 tbsp caster sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ½ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Mix wet
steps.text: Whisk 1 large egg and 42 g unsalted butter (melted and cooled slightly) into the milk, pour into a well in the flour and whisk very gently until just combined (a few lumps).

steps.title: Heat pan
steps.text: Heat a 30 cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat for 3-5 min, add 1 tsp vegetable oil and brush it over.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour 60 ml batter in 3 places and sprinkle each with 1 tbsp blueberries (fresh or frozen, rinsed and dried, wild if possible). Cook until large bubbles appear (1½-2 min); flip and cook until golden (1-1½ min more). Serve at once; repeat, using the remaining oil only if needed.

tips: Lemon juice curdled into milk mimics buttermilk, tenderising the pancakes and adding a subtle tang that brightens the fruit.
Wild blueberries are smaller and more flavourful than cultivated ones; use them if you can find them.
Pat the blueberries dry before using them; any excess water streaks the batter and makes the pancakes soggy.
storage: Best served fresh and warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
